resources.string: GMI is taking applications for Diploma and GAPP. Tap to apply online.
A UTeM degree on GMI\'s campus
Bachelor of Electrical Engineering Technology with Honours, taught at GMI.
Top in the world for A-Level Mathematics
Cambridge Learner Awards in 2010, 2013, 2017 and 2019. See GAPP.
A GMI campus building, seen from a courtyard
Each department has its own workshops, labs and studios. The campus also has a library, sports facilities, hostels and a surau. Swipe a row of photos, or tap one to see it full screen.
Industry-standard labs, many set up with partners such as ZEISS, Emerson and Cisco
GMI\'s 360° tour lets you look around these places on campus:
Photos © German-Malaysian Institute, from gmi.edu.my, used for this student project.
CNC workshops, a machine shop, metal stamping, ZEISS measuring equipment and 3D printers.
Labs for autotronics, digital electronics and process control, with Emerson and Siemens control systems.
Computer, network and cyber security labs, plus multimedia, post-production and cinematic studios.
Classrooms, a chemistry lab and a lecture hall.
Study spaces and books on campus. Students can also use GMI\'s e-book collection, the U-Pustaka digital library, GMI\'s institutional repository and online dictionaries.
A gymnasium, a badminton hall, an indoor futsal court, tennis courts, a football field and a netball court.
On-campus rooms. For Malaysian diploma students the hostel is optional and costs RM900 a semester. Fees are subject to change.
The campus prayer hall, named Surau An-Najah in GMI\'s virtual tour.
GMI says it has 22 Advanced Technology Centres. These are the ones with their own page on GMI\'s website.
GMI also runs international exams on campus.
A series of high-end CNC machines for training in making complex parts, such as those used in aerospace, automotive, oil and gas, and medical industries.
Set up with ZEISS for precise dimensional measurement and quality inspection using Coordinate Measuring Machines (CMMs).
Robot programming with a teach pendant and in offline simulation, with real industrial applications in each robot workcell.
Product Lifecycle Management software that combines CAD, CAM and CAE, so design, machining and simulation can each be done as a digital twin for Industry 4.0.
Opened on 4 October 2018 with LVD equipment for sheet metal CAD/CAM, cutting and bending, including a CNC press brake.
Plastic injection moulding training, from the basics to advanced troubleshooting and maintenance. The trainers are certified by the German Training Centre (Asia).
Courses in basic and proportional hydraulics, the technology behind much of the machinery in construction, production and packaging.
A process control setup with automation and operator stations, field instruments and a mini-scale plant, run on Siemens PCS 7.
The same kind of process control setup, run on Emerson DeltaV. Participants configure control strategies, create alarms and troubleshoot the system.
Training in instrument specification, calibration and maintenance, with flow and level calibration rigs, ending in a valid calibration report.
A Cisco Networking Academy since 2011, with switches, routers, ASA firewalls and VoIP phones for hands-on CCNA training.
Hands-on learning about the most common cyber threats, attacks and vulnerabilities, and how businesses protect themselves.
GMI is a Cambridge examination centre for GCE A-Level, the qualification GAPP prepares for.
A TELC certified centre for German language exams.
GMI also hosts IELTS English exams and runs an IELTS preparatory course.
GMI lists these loans, scholarships and grants for its students. Each sponsor sets its own rules and makes its own decision.
Financial aid is only for Malaysian students for now.
You can hold only one education loan or scholarship at a time.
Only the sponsor can approve a loan or scholarship. GMI cannot approve or guarantee one.
Tap a sponsor to see the details.
For help with applications: 03-8921 9008 / 9013 or sponsorship@gmi.edu.my
Amounts are as GMI lists them. Some dates on GMI\'s page are from 2025, so check the current dates with each sponsor before you apply.

string-array.name: aid_scheme_bodies
string-array.item: For diploma and degree students. If your parents earn RM12,000 a month or less (or RM150,000 a year in taxable income), it covers your study fees plus RM730 a month for living costs. From RM12,001 to RM20,000 a month (RM150,001 to RM250,000 a year), it covers study fees only. Apply through GMI\'s TESP page and MARA\'s education loan portal.
For GAPP students. Covers study fees and a living allowance at GMI and in Germany, plus flights between Malaysia and Germany.

Diploma students apply from 2 January to 28 February, or 1 July to 31 August. GUFP students apply in September or October through GMI\'s Loan & Sponsorship Unit, using their UTP offer letter. PTPTN sets the eligibility and amounts.
For Computer & Information diploma students with at least 5 As in SPM. RM11,000 a year. It usually opens in August.
A bank education loan for Malaysians aged 18 to 45, with family members as co-applicants. It can pay for semesters or fees that PTPTN, MARA or similar aid do not cover.

MAIPk, Perak: RM1,000 one-off for diploma students
MAINS, Negeri Sembilan: RM1,000 one-off for new diploma students
MUIP, Pahang: RM700 or RM800 one-off for students born in Pahang
MAIK, Kelantan: RM1,000 to RM2,000 one-off for eligible asnaf students
MAIDAM, Terengganu: education aid for asnaf miskin and fisabilillah students
MAIJ, Johor: RM1,000 one-off at registration for low-income families
Lembaga Zakat Selangor: help with fees and living costs for asnaf fakir and miskin
Each council has its own rules on where you live and your family's income.

JPA Sabah and Yayasan Sabah: scholarships and loans for diploma and degree study\nMUIS Sabah: aid for asnaf, fakir, miskin and mualaf students\nSabah Deputy State Secretary\'s Office: RM1,500 one-off registration aid for diploma students from B40 families
For Malaysians recognised as Orang Asli, aged 35 or under, who do not already have another scholarship, bursary or loan.
